q-131244.name: Question 1
q-131244.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)\,i+x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)\,j-x{z}^{4}\,k.
$$
q-131244.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F)=\frac{3}{2}∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-x{z}^{4}) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3} \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F) & =\frac{3}{2}∇\cdot F \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3}) \\  & =6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-6x{z}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-131245.name: Question 2
q-131245.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}{y}^{3}\,i+{y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,j,\,∇\cdot G=-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x).
$$
q-131245.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+4G) & =∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)+∇\cdot (4G) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F+2G) & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F+4∇\cdot G \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x{y}^{3}+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+4\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & =x{y}^{3}+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =x{y}^{3}-y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-41842.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (F+2G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{2}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}.
$$

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F+2G) & =∇\cdot F+∇\cdot (2G) \\  & =∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2y}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F+2G) & =∇\cdot F+2∇\cdot G \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}+2\cdot (-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{y}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{y}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2y}{{y}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(1+y)}{{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-105634.name: Question 5
q-105634.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (-3F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,j-4z\,k.
$$
q-105634.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-3F) & =-3∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(4z) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4 \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4 \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-3F) & =-3∇\cdot F \\  & =-3\cdot 2(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2) \\  & =6(2-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

q-98888.name: Question 6
q-98888.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨y,x⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)=1+{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =xy(1+{x}^{2})+⟨x,{x}^{2}y⟩\cdot ⟨y,x⟩ \\  & =xy+{x}^{3}y+xy+{x}^{3}y \\  & =2xy+2{x}^{3}y \\  & =2xy(1+{x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Given that F(x,y)=⟨x,x2y⟩ and f(x,y)=xy, calculate ∇⋅(fF).

a
2xy(1+xy)
b
2xy(1+x2)
c
2xy(1+x)
d
2xy(1+y2)
e
2xy(1+y3)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the following identity:

∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f

First, we compute ∇⋅F and ∇f. We get

∇f=⟨y,x⟩,∇⋅F=∂∂x(x)+∂∂y(x2y)=1+x2.

Therefore, we have ∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f=xy(1+x2)+⟨x,x2y⟩⋅⟨y,x⟩=xy+x3y+xy+x3y=2xy+2x3y=2xy(1+x2).

q-105656.name: Question 7
q-105656.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨yz,xz,xy⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(zy)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(zx)=y+z+x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =xyz(x+y+z)+⟨xy,zy,zx⟩\cdot ⟨yz,xz,xy⟩ \\  & =xyz(x+y+z)+x{y}^{2}z+xy{z}^{2}+{x}^{2}yz \\  & =xyz(x+y+z)+xyz(x+y+z) \\  & =2xyz(x+y+z).\end{aligned}
$$

q-131289.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨1,1,-1⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2})=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =(x+y-z)\cdot 0+⟨{y}^{2}z,{x}^{2}+z,{x}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\  & =0+{y}^{2}z+{x}^{2}+z-{x}^{2} \\  & ={y}^{2}z+z \\  & =z({y}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Given that F(x,y,z)=⟨y2z,x2+z,x2⟩ and f(x,y,z)=x+y−z, calculate ∇⋅(fF).

a
z(xy2+z)
b
z(xy2−1)
c
z(y2+x)
d
z(y+1)
e
z(y2+1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the following identity:

∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f

First, we compute ∇⋅F and ∇f. We get

∇f=⟨1,1,−1⟩,∇⋅F=∂∂x(y2z)+∂∂y(x2+z)+∂∂z(x2)=0.

Therefore, we have ∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f=(x+y−z)⋅0+⟨y2z,x2+z,x2⟩⋅⟨1,1,−1⟩=0+y2z+x2+z−x2=y2z+z=z(y2+1).

q-131288.name: Question 9
q-131288.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨{e}^{y},x{e}^{y}⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)=y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =x{e}^{y}(y+1)+⟨xy,y⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{y},x{e}^{y}⟩ \\  & =xy{e}^{y}+x{e}^{y}+xy{e}^{y}+xy{e}^{y} \\  & =3xy{e}^{y}+x{e}^{y} \\  & =x(3y+1){e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that F(x,y)=⟨xy,2y⟩ and f(x,y)=x2y, calculate ∇⋅(fF).

a
x2y(3y+4)
b
x2(3y2+2)
c
x2(3y+2x)
d
xy(xy+2x)
e
x2y(y+2x+2)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the following identity:

∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f

First, we compute ∇⋅F and ∇f. We get

∇f=⟨2xy,x2⟩,∇⋅F=∂∂x(xy)+∂∂y(2y)=y+2.

Therefore, we have ∇⋅(fF)=f∇⋅F+F⋅∇f=x2y(y+2)+⟨xy,2y⟩⋅⟨2xy,x2⟩=x2y2+2x2y+2x2y2+2x2y=3x2y2+4x2y=x2y(3y+4).
